name: Fever in Children (under 5)
source_guidance: Adapted from WHO Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) general danger signs and classification of fever and cough, and WHO malaria guidelines.

questions.text: Is the child having a fit now, or has the child had a fit during this illness?
Is the child unusually sleepy, hard to wake, or unconscious?
Is the child unable to drink or breastfeed, or vomiting everything?
Is the baby younger than 2 months?
Is the child struggling to breathe, making a harsh noise when breathing in while calm, or are the lips blue?
Is there a rash that does not fade when a glass is pressed on it, or a stiff neck?
Is the child breathing fast, or does the lower chest pull in with each breath?
Has the fever lasted more than two days?
Has the child not yet had a malaria test for this fever?

emergency: Call 112 now, or get to the nearest hospital emergency department immediately.
Take the child to the nearest hospital now. These are danger signs.
Keep breastfeeding or giving sips of fluid on the way if the child is awake and able to swallow.
Do not put anything in the child's mouth during a fit. Lay the child on their side.
Keep the child lightly dressed, not wrapped in heavy cloth.
urgent: Take the child to a clinic or primary health centre today.
Ask for a malaria test before any malaria medicine is given.
Keep breastfeeding and give extra fluids.
Return at once or call 112 if the child cannot drink, vomits everything, has a fit, or becomes very sleepy.
self_care: The child has a fever with no danger signs and has already tested negative for malaria.
Keep breastfeeding and give extra fluids.
Dress the child lightly. Paracetamol can be given using the dose for the child's age or weight on the pack.
Make sure the child sleeps under an insecticide-treated mosquito net.
Call back or go to a clinic if the fever lasts more than two days or any danger sign appears.
